comments.author: @BroOmnipotent
comments.text:
I've got a mystery story about a month ago. Normally my phone is on silent, and I'm rarely picking up unless I specifically expect an important call (or it's a short list of very close people who are marked as exceptions even to silent mode, and each of whom I'll tell from any kind of AI voice, however perfect, in first couple phrases) - the normal protocol is message me first. But, well, i was just scrolling something, called ID showed my cellular company, so I did.
Nice person here introduced herself as support, and notified me that a) my phone number contract is about to expire b) they do not need any card information or anything from me, they only need my approval if I want to extend it.
Now the red barn is quite obvious, but a subtle thing is, once upon a time, it was a variation - also kinda scammy - but done by legit cellular providers around here, because your OK on the phone can be binding. 
Anyways, I said I'm on the go, which was true, and that I approve, extend the way it was. Oke, told me the lady, we'll need to go through further motions with you on this, when our *some kinda persons* can contact you? All right, in an hour. 

As said, I WAS on the go, from neighborhood groacery store to a local craft bar. What I did not elaborate is, just so happens, in a big mall right between those two spots are, guess what, small sales-and-service office of my cellular. So I literally was there 5 minutes later.

Kinda unsurprisingly, there were no problems on my account, they never heard of such an issue about "phone number expiring". So they quite clearly instructed me to cut the communication.
However, they also did not know what kinda scam that was.
As in, I guess it should've ended up with either asking for my card or other "means", or for that "confirmation code you just got on the sms". I aint born yesterday.
But the lady really wasn't pushing for neither. At least during the talk we had.

Also, I've been denied all the fun, cuz noone contacted me "in an hour" or at any time. Obviously nothing "expired" either.

Like, wtf was it? The initiation was almost textbook (you've got an emergency "problem", we are the good official legit guys, just do as we say and we'll help yhou through it), but it absolutely lacked the part where I am asked to actually "open up". Nowhere not a normal hasty and pushy way. I mean, that lady absolutely, no argument, allowed me to cool off the phone for an hour. That's NOT how to run such scams.
Maybe she was just new, and they - those scam operations are rarely just 1-2 persons - didn't bother calling back because realized she blundered it already?
